description: The key name 'wallet' is reused across this feature's own artifacts with THREE mutually incompatible shapes, and the spec -- despite explicitly and repeatedly disambiguating a closely related field (walletAddress vs wallet in citizens.json, the entire resolution of FIND-104) -- never once flags or disambiguates this second collision. (1) child-spec.js::buildChildSpec's real, existing, unmodified returned row stores wallet as a bare STRING (the child's own address): 'wallet: childWallet' (child-spec.js:37), confirmed by its own test fixture (child-spec.test.js:36: assert.strictEqual(spec.wallet, '0xCHILD...')). REQ-206/REQ-305 both route through this exact function/row shape unmodified. (2) REQ-105/citizens.json's registry record defines wallet as a BOOLEAN presence-flag OBJECT: '{evm?: boolean, solana?: boolean}' -- explicitly NOT an address. (3) REQ-105's own SEPARATE walletAddress field carries the actual address STRING(s) for citizens.json. So within the SAME feature's own diff, 'wallet' means 'an address string' in one file (ledger.js rows, via child-spec.js) and 'a pair of booleans' in another (citizens.json), while the semantic equivalent of ledger.js's wallet field (an address string) is called walletAddress, not wallet, in citizens.json. A fresh implementer cross-referencing REQ-206's derivation table against REQ-105's registry schema in the same sitting has a concrete, evidenced opportunity to conflate these -- exactly the class of confusion FIND-104's entire resolution (splitting wallet/walletAddress in ONE file) was designed to close, left open in the adjacent file this same spec also modifies.

evidence.snippet: return { child_id: childId, wallet: childWallet, parent_wallet: parentWallet, ... }

'wallet: {evm?: boolean, solana?: boolean} -- a presence-flag pair...'; 'walletAddress: {evm?: string, solana?: string} -- the actual address string(s)... this field is NEVER passed to isSelfFunded()'
